subject: Recap & next steps: inference economics and pilot fit
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@ledgerly.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-08-30T16:12:00-07:00
Subject: Recap & next steps: inference economics and pilot fit

Elena — thanks for taking the time earlier. Quick written recap so we have the same working assumptions and a clear set of next steps.

Call summary (30 min)
- Primary pain: per-request token costs are unpredictable at scale and are materially impacting go-to-market economics for your conversational product.
- Latency target: 95th percentile target is ~150ms for most user-facing flows; spikes during peak hours are an issue today.
- Current volume: ~1.2–1.6M tokens/day across regionally routed traffic (US).
- Budget constraint: procurement signaled ~<$30k/mo for inference until we prove savings vs current self-hosted approach.
- Compliance: must support audit logs and VPC option; SOC 2 evidence will be required during SOW.

Key levers we discussed that move the needle on TCO
- Batching and request coalescing (best for high-concurrency generate flows)
- Prefix/KV caching for prompt-heavy patterns (saves repeated decoding cost)
- Quantized model variants for non-critical generation paths
- Routing lower-priority calls to cheaper model variants or burst pools

Proposed pilot (6 weeks, low risk)
- Scope: 2 endpoints (chat & summarization), Redwood-hosted, dedicated pool for predictable throughput.
- Test volume: target 1.5M tokens/day to mirror your peak; will run A/B with current infra on a subset of traffic.
- Goals: demonstrate unit-cost reduction (tokens/$) and confirm 95p latency SLOs.
- Deliverables: weekly cost snapshots, latency heatmaps, and a TCO comparison report at pilot end.

Attachments: redwood-pilot-worksheet.xlsx (pilot sizing + estimated cost scenarios), ledgerly-tco-snapshot.pdf (initial TCO headlines)

Asks / next steps
1) Can you confirm the budget ceiling ($30k/mo) and whether we should engineer proposals around that constraint?
2) Please confirm stakeholders for legal/Security (for SOC 2/contracting) and an engineering lead we should loop in for kickoff.
3) If that looks good, I’ll send a short SOW + pilot worksheet and propose two kickoff windows next week.

Available slots for kickoff: Tue 9/2 10:00–11:00 PT or Wed 9/3 14:00–15:00 PT.

Thanks — looking forward to aligning.

Best,
Ben Carter
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com | (415) 555-0182

Ben — appreciate the clear write-up. Quick confirmations and clarifications from our side:

- Budget: procurement confirmed an initial runway of up to $30k/mo for the pilot phase, but we need a clear fail/upgrade trigger tied to demonstrated unit-cost savings.
- Latency: 150ms 95p is a hard requirement for chat; summarization can tolerate higher latency if cost savings materialize.
- Compliance: Security wants to see SOC 2 in-progress evidence + ability to route through our VPC.

Stakeholders to include: Rohan Mehta (ENG manager — cc’d), Priya Natarajan (Security) — I’ll introduce Priya once legal gets closer to SOW.

Two asks:
1) Can you send the pilot worksheet filled with a scenario that targets $25k/mo (aggressive) and a conservative $35k/mo scenario so Procurement can see the range?
2) Can you include an explicit rollback/fallback plan in case latency SLO is missed during peak?

Kickoff: Wed 9/3 14:00 PT works for Rohan and me.

Thanks,
Elena
Head of Product — Ledgerly
elena.ruiz@ledgerly.com

Elena / Rohan — thanks for the quick turnaround and clear asks. Short response to both items below and updated attachments.

1) Budget scenarios: attached I’ve included three pre-filled scenarios in redwood-pilot-worksheet.xlsx:
   - Aggressive target: $25k/mo (higher batching and aggressive cache settings; uses 8-bit quantized variant for background flows)
   - Baseline: $30k/mo (what we discussed)
   - Conservative: $35k/mo (less batching, higher headroom for latency SLOs)

2) Rollback/fallback: pilot will include an automatic routing policy that (a) routes latency-sensitive requests to a higher-tier pool (slightly higher cost) when 95p latency drifts beyond 150ms, and (b) a hard failover to your existing endpoints for a configurable percentage of traffic if we miss SLO for >3 consecutive peak windows. I captured that in the SOW draft (redwood-pilot-sow-draft.docx).

3) Compliance/Access: we can provide SOC 2 in-progress evidence and set up a VPC peering plan for the pilot. I’ll loop in our security lead if Priya asks for specifics.

Next steps (action items)
- I’ll upload the worksheet and SOW draft to the HubSpot deal record: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/1234567/LDG-4832
- Please confirm kickoff for Wed 9/3 14:00 PT — I’ll send a calendar invite and a short list of integration tasks (JWTs, endpoints, sample payloads).
- Once kickoff is scheduled, I’ll request Connor (solutions architect) join the call to scope integration effort.

Attachments: redwood-pilot-worksheet.xlsx, redwood-pilot-sow-draft.docx

Ben
